description: Modern banking in India began in the late 18th century. After independence, to ensure economic equality, financial inclusion, and adequate credit flow to agriculture and small industries, the Government of India nationalized major commercial banks.

sections.title: Early Banking History
sections.description: Details of the first banks established during the British era and the early banks started with Indian capital.

historical_events.significance: It was the first bank of India, established by the European agency house Alexander & Co. in Calcutta.
It was the first commercial bank with limited liability that was entirely managed by Indians.
It was the first bank established completely with Indian capital, founded by Lala Lajpat Rai.

historical_events.event: Formation of Imperial Bank of India
historical_events.significance: Created by merging the three Presidency Banks: Bank of Bengal (1806), Bank of Bombay (1840), and Bank of Madras (1843).

sections.title: Development of RBI and SBI
sections.description: The evolutionary journey of India's Central Bank and its largest Public Sector Bank.

key_concepts.explanation: An apex financial institution that regulates the country's money supply, monetary policy, and the commercial banking system.

historical_events.event: Establishment of Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
historical_events.significance: Established under the RBI Act 1934 based on the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission.
Post-independence, the Reserve Bank of India was brought entirely under the ownership of the Government of India.

historical_events.event: Formation of State Bank of India (SBI)
historical_events.significance: On the recommendation of the A.D. Gorewala Committee, the Imperial Bank of India was nationalized and renamed as SBI.

important_facts.fact: Sir Osborne Smith was the first Governor of the RBI, while C.D. Deshmukh was the first Indian Governor.

sections.title: First Phase of Nationalization (1969)
sections.description: The large-scale government takeover of private banks aiming for social control and financial inclusion.

key_concepts.explanation: The process of transferring private sector assets, industries, or banks into public ownership and state control.

historical_events.significance: A historic step taken during Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's tenure to expand banking networks into unbanked rural areas.

important_facts.fact: The main criterion for the first phase of nationalization in 1969 was that the bank's total deposits must exceed 50 Crore Rupees.

sections.title: Second Phase of Nationalization and Subsequent Reforms
sections.description: Further expansion of the banking sector in the 1980s and the transformations post the 1991 economic reforms.

historical_events.significance: The total number of nationalized banks reached 20. The criterion for this phase was a deposit base of over 200 Crore Rupees.
This committee recommended comprehensive banking sector reforms, including the licensing of new private sector banks.

historical_events.event: Merger of New Bank of India
historical_events.significance: The New Bank of India was merged into the Punjab National Bank (PNB), reducing the total number of nationalized banks from 20 to 19.

sections.title: Recent Mergers and Current Status
sections.description: The mega-mergers of Public Sector Banks (PSBs) initiated to create global-sized, robust banking institutions.

historical_events.significance: Consolidated 10 public sector banks into 4 larger and more efficient entities to strengthen the banking system.

key_associations.item: Oriental Bank of Commerce and United Bank of India
key_associations.extra_info: Post-merger, PNB became the second-largest Public Sector Bank in India.
This merger made Canara Bank the fourth-largest PSB in the country.
Allahabad Bank was one of the oldest joint-stock banks in India prior to its merger.

important_facts.fact: Following all the recent merger processes, the total number of Public Sector Banks (PSBs) currently operating in India is 12.
The State Bank of India (SBI) remains the largest commercial bank in India in terms of total assets and branch network.
